newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Daewoo plans $25 mln Romania bank JV.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo plans $25 mln Romania bank JV.

text.p: Daewoo Securities Co, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, said on Thursday it was seeking to set up a $25 million joint venture bank in Romania.
"We are waiting for South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy to approve the venture before signing the deal," said a Daewoo Group spokesman.

Daewoo Securities said in a statement it would hold a 89.99 percent stake in the venture, temporarily named "Daewoo Bank (Romania) S.A.", while South Korea's Koram Bank would take 10 percent and four Romanian investors the rest.
The statement said Daewoo chose Romania on expectations of growth in that country's economy and financial industry.
The joint venture would also help provide funds for Korean companies in Romania, it said.
Daewoo said it also was considering buying a state-run bank in France which was been privatised. Company officials declined to name the bank.
